belief: I must give people whatever they ask of me.
origins: Generous people, caregivers, and helpers can be asked for time, money, rides, listening, and favors without end. If we were raised to think that refusing a request is unloving, we can end up drained and used. Some of us also feel that if someone is in need, we are automatically responsible.
teaches: Paul writes of giving, “Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.” He also says, “Each one should carry his own load.” Proverbs notes, “The prudent man watches his steps.” Jesus said, “Let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes,’ and your ‘No,’ ‘No.’” Giving is a gift of the heart. It is not a duty to anyone who asks. We are called to love, and love uses wisdom: sometimes it gives, sometimes it says no, and sometimes it points to other resources.
self_statements: If someone asks, I have to say yes.
I cannot say no to people in need.
If I do not help, no one will.
errors: Insisting that I must meet every request.
Treating every need as my responsibility.
Believing I must give everything or nothing.
questions: What do people ask of me that leaves me resentful?
Do I give out of cheerful choice or compulsion?
What are my real limits in time, money, and energy?
What are other resources the person could use?
How can I say no with kindness?
What would giving freely look like?
truth: I am free to decide what I give. God loves a cheerful giver, not a compelled one. I can say yes with joy when I can, say no with kindness when I cannot, and trust God to care for those I cannot help.
hw_truths: I decide in my heart what to give.
I can trust God with others’ needs.
log: Each week, record one thing you gave gladly and one request you declined kindly.
actions: Write the requests that leave you resentful.
Decide what you can give in time and money.
Write, “I can’t, but I hope you find help.”
Choose one thing to give freely this week.
prayer: Lord, I want to be generous, but I am worn out. Teach me to give freely and wisely, to say no kindly, and to trust You with the needs I cannot meet. Amen.
hw_questions: Do I give gladly or by compulsion?
How can I say no kindly?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I decide in my heart what to give, and God loves a cheerful giver.”
